newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany against "Keynesian" boost to EU jobs.
newsitem.headline: Germany against "Keynesian" boost to EU jobs.

text.p: Germany will continue to resist any European Union employment chapter that it judges to be based on short-term cash injections rather than longer-term structural solutions, a government spokesman said on Friday.

"What we opposed are moth-eaten measures out of the Keynesian bag of tricks," a spokesman told a regular government news briefing, referring to the British economist who promoted growth policies based on boosting economic demand.
"We are against any employment chapter with just a placebo effect," he added.

Bonn, concerned that it might have to foot much of the bill for any such plan, has looked increasingly isolated in its opposition to an employment chapter due to be discussed the June 16 summit on EU treaty reforms in Amsterdam.
EU partners including Britain and France have both proposed job creation schemes in recent days, with measures such as giving aid to small and medium firms to provide more jobs.
German opposition parties and trade union groups have meanwhile increased the domestic pressure on Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government to agree to an employment chapter.

But Hans Apel, a former German finance minister and member of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said any employment chapter that needed serious funding was unlikely given the weak current state of many EU national budgets.
"I just can't see how any such programme could be financed... Any Brussels initiatives can only really have a voluntary character," he told German radio on Friday.
The German Federal Labour Office earlier reported a 56,000 increase in seasonally-adjusted May unemployment.
